visible_difference: Today the far bank is drawn as four stacked limestone strips. Each runs the full creek width of 1800 units and has a ruled bottom edge, and the grass band above them also has a ruled lower edge. Read at phone size, the result is a set of straight horizontal bands just under the grass and at the water's far edge. The replacement redraws that bank as broken limestone ledges that step, end partway across and vary in thickness. Slumped blocks and vegetation cover the joints, and the grass meets the stone along a ragged edge. The stated test is that no near-straight run longer than about 150 units remains. This changes a different layer (CreekBack, plus the water's far edge listed in the notes) from the shelf patch that pivot 3 retired. It is not a rename, an easing change or a camera offset.
source_basis: The bank's shape carries no factual claim. Claims c3 and c4 (the April 20th account: an unoccupied car at a creek's shallow edge, carried downstream, with no crossing shown) are unchanged. So are the disclosure chip and the Bexar County setting of Salado Creek under live oaks. Broken, stepped limestone ledges are an ordinary feature of San Antonio creek banks and fit the region plate. The drawing stays a disclosed illustration and adds nothing about damage, depth or how the car reached the edge.
